text: Given message_id="m1" and user_id="u1", When graph_delete_message is called, Then the server requests DELETE /users/u1/messages/m1 and the result is {"user_id": "u1", "message_id": "m1", "deleted": true}
Given message_id="m1" and no user_id, When graph_delete_message is called, Then the server requests DELETE /me/messages/m1 and the result is {"user_id": "me", "message_id": "m1", "deleted": true}
Given a message_id for which the Graph client raises a 404 GraphError, When graph_delete_message is called, Then the result is still {"deleted": true}, not an error envelope

Given a message_id for which the Graph client raises a 403 GraphError, When graph_delete_message is called, Then the result is the structured error envelope with the mapped error code, and no "deleted": true is returned

Given the server's registered tool list, When graph_delete_message is inspected, Then its required parameters are exactly {message_id}, and its annotations are readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true, idempotentHint=true

Given the repo's tests/test_gdap_role_map.py consistency test, When it runs after this change, Then it still passes -- graph_delete_message has matching entries in EXPECTED_TOOLS, the README Tools table, and docs/gdap-role-map.yaml

Given no live Microsoft 365 tenant/test mailbox is available at design time, When graph_delete_message is self-tested, Then it is run once against a disposable test message on whatever tenant is available during the dev leg and the outcome (pass, or needs-real-tenant) is recorded in README Known Gaps -- per mcp-track.md 2.5, the absence of a test account is not a blocker
steps: During the dev/self-test leg, on a tenant with a real Microsoft Graph connection, send a disposable test email to a test mailbox
Call graph_list_messages to find its message_id
Confirm in Outlook/OWA that the message moved to Deleted Items
expect: graph_delete_message returns {"deleted": true}; the test message is visible in Deleted Items, not the original folder
